page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance within the VX1 family, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single AMD EPYC physical core operating at 2.0 GHz. The processor features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB shared L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. It provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, combined with a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD boot volume and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU acceleration is included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded processing capabilities alongside distinct multi-threaded bottlenecks inherent to the dual-vCPU constraint. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests and compression benchmarks, logging 39.39 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.44 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Geekbench single-core performance registers an average score of 1775.0. However, multi-core throughput remains in the lower quartile across tests such as PassMark CPU (4920.93) and Geekbench multi-core (2261.0), as well as Clang compilation (2713.0) and ray tracing (2816.0), where parallel execution is bound by the two-thread limit.

Memory subsystem throughput is balanced, maintaining average large-block sequential read and write transfers of 45.11 GB/sec and 39.66 GB/sec, matching its PassMark memory score of 2188.13. Networked static web serving sustains an average throughput of 7.66 GB/sec, while low-concurrency Redis SET operations achieve 4.06 million operations per second. Light inference workloads on small 135M parameter language models sustain text generation at 119.62 tokens per second, but performance degrades heavily on larger 7B models at 6.65 tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance delivers high memory density per core without requiring high CPU core licensing. The minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD limits self-contained local storage capacity, requiring secondary block storage for data-heavy operations. The server fits memory-resident background workers, caching proxies, lightweight in-memory databases, and memory-heavy batch jobs with moderate concurrent compute demands.
description: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single AMD EPYC physical core running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory and a 1 GB NVMe SSD boot drive. With an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation, the configuration prioritizes RAM density. Single-threaded benchmarks are strong, showing top-tier performance in single-core stress tests, gzip compression (39.39 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.44 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate parallel throughput is constrained by the two-thread topology, resulting in bottom-quartile scores in multi-core Geekbench and PassMark CPU suites. Memory bandwidth remains solid with large-block reads measuring 45.11 GB/sec. Given its high RAM allocation relative to compute capability and negligible local disk capacity, this server is suitable for memory-intensive caching layers, lightweight in-memory data processing, and single-threaded batch workers requiring ample RAM.
